bull.t: Strong product demand and revenue growth
bull.b: Strong demand across VEVYE, IHEEZO, and TRIESENCE indicates broadening commercial traction rather than reliance on one product. Rising prescriptions, ordering accounts, and surgical adoption can support durable revenue expansion as sales coverage and market access continue to improve.

bull.t: High-margin economics and improving cash generation
bull.b: Positive operating and free cash flow marks a meaningful improvement from prior periods and provides internal funding for commercialization. Combined with very high gross margins and expected mix and pricing benefits, this supports liquidity and the potential for operating leverage.

bull.t: Broader ophthalmic portfolio and market access
bull.b: Adding TYRVAYA broadens Harrow’s dry-eye offering and gives physicians another treatment format, while expanded PBM coverage can enlarge the addressable patient base. A wider portfolio and stronger access may improve commercial productivity and reinforce its ophthalmic position.

bear.t: Elevated leverage and thin equity cushion
bear.b: Higher debt alongside a sharply reduced equity cushion limits financial flexibility if performance weakens. It also makes refinancing, dilution, and capital allocation more consequential, requiring sustained cash generation to support obligations and gradually reduce balance-sheet risk.

bear.t: Ongoing losses and elevated operating costs
bear.b: The gap between strong gross margins and continued net losses suggests that operating costs or non-operating items remain substantial. Until revenue growth converts consistently into earnings, Harrow has less capacity to self-fund expansion and remains exposed to execution setbacks.

The reimbursement change removes an important route for IHEEZO adoption in ambulatory surgery centers and constrains access in that setting. Although Harrow is shifting toward in-office markets, the lost channel can limit product penetration and make growth more dependent on execution elsewhere.
